name: Falciparum malaria, carried by Anopheles mosquitoes
_doc: As trypanosomiasis.json. Host 'people': annual_loss_at_full_challenge is an excess death rate per year for each demography band (children, working_age, elderly), added to baseline mortality and scaled by the disease burden the nation has not yet removed.

challenge_envelope.source: Temperature: Mordecai et al. 2013 Ecology Letters 16:22, abstract via USGS (pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70125667): 'predicts optimal malaria transmission at 25 C' and 'transmission decreases dramatically at temperatures > 28 C'; the 17 to 34 C limits are quoted from Ryan et al. (arXiv 1407.7612): 'temperatures between 17-34 C (Mordecai et al. 2013)'. The 22 to 28 C optimum band is centred on the 25 C optimum (+-3 C, upper edge at the 28 C decline), derived. Rainfall: Smith et al. 2020 (Nature Communications, PMC7455692, opened) apply Craig et al. 1999 as a monthly threshold of '80 mm month-1' and an 18 C monthly minimum. Derived annual edges: 80 mm in every month is 960 mm, taken as the 1000 mm lower optimum edge; 80 mm in only the wettest five months is 400 mm, the tolerated lower edge (five months is an assumption). The 4000 and 6000 mm upper edges have no source (stand-in).

hosts.people.source: Malaria deaths before control fell mostly on children under five in holoendemic areas, of order one to two percent of them a year, a few per thousand of adults who have acquired partial immunity (Snow et al. 2005 Nature 434:214; Hay et al. 2004). No pre-industrial death register exists, so the rates are an order of magnitude only.
